entries.answer:
Az Exa AI egy teljesen újraépített, neurális hálózatokon alapuló keresőmotor, amelyet kifejezetten AIalkalmazások és nagy nyelvi modellek (LLMek) számára terveztek – nem hagyományos kulcsszavas keresésre, hanem szemantikai megértésre optimalizálva.

 Az alapvető neurális architektúra

Az Exa legfontosabb technológiai újítása egy endtoend neurális hálózat, amelynek középpontjában egy ún. link prediction transformer áll. Ez azt jelenti, hogy az indexelés és a visszakeresés minden lépése neurális modelleken keresztül történik – szemben a hagyományos keresők (pl. Google) PageRankalapú, linkgráf és kulcsszóegyeztetéses megközelítésével. A rendszer az embeddingek (vektoros reprezentációk) segítségével tárolja a weboldalak szemantikai tartalmát, így a lekérdezések során nem szó szerinti egyezést keres, hanem fogalmi hasonlóságot.[1][2]

Az index folyamatosan frissül: a keresési index percenkénti frissítéssel biztosítja, hogy az AIalkalmazások valóban naprakész információhoz jussanak. Az indexelés során az Exa automatikusan eltávolítja a navigációs elemeket, hirdetéseket és cookieértesítőket, így csak a tiszta, tartalmi szöveg kerül be az adatbázisba – ez az előfeldolgozás indexidőben, nem lekérdezésidőben történik, ami kulcsfontosságú a gyors válaszidő szempontjából.[3][2]

 Saját GPU infrastruktúra

Az Exa az iparágban szokatlan, merész döntést hozott: már a cég korai szakaszában (78 fős csapatnál) saját GPUklasztert vásárolt ahelyett, hogy felhőszolgáltatókra támaszkodott volna. Jelenleg egy 144 db NVIDIA H200 GPUból álló új klasztert és egy meglévő 80 db A100 GPUs klasztert üzemeltet párhuzamosan. Az infrastruktúrastack öt rétegből áll: Pulumi (infrastruktúrakód), Ansible/Kubespray (szerverkonfiguráció), NVIDIA operátorok, Alluxio (elosztott tárolás) és Flyte (MLpipelineok orkesztrációja).[4][5]

 Lekérdezésfeldolgozás és keresési módok

Az Exa intelligensen kombinálja a neurális és a kulcsszavas keresést: a rendszer a lekérdezés jellegétől függően automatikusan választja ki a legjobb megközelítést. A természetes nyelvű kérdéseket a rendszer gépi reprezentációvá alakítja, és a transformerarchitektúra segítségével szemantikai értelmet rendel hozzájuk, lehetővé téve az összetett, többrétegű kérdések feldolgozását is.[6]

 APItermékarchitektúra

Az Exa négy fő APIvégpontot kínál fejlesztők számára, amelyek különböző AIalkalmazási igényeket elégítenek ki.[4]

| Végpont | Kimenet | Felhasználási eset |
||||
| /search (csak URLek) | URLlisták | Ultraalacsony késleltetésű alkalmazások |
| /search (URL + tartalom) | URL + teljes Markdown szöveg | LLMek számára RAG pipelineok |
| /answer | Strukturált válasz vagy riport | Előfeldolgozott, kész válaszok |
| /research | Komplex struktúrált kimenet | Agentic, mélykutatási feladatok |

 Multiagent kutatási rendszer

Az Exa /research végpontja egy LangGraphalapú multiagent architektúrát alkalmaz. Egy Planner ágens feldarabolja a komplex lekérdezést részfeladatokra, több párhuzamos Task ágens hajtja végre ezeket egyidejűleg Exakereséssel, majd egy Observer ágens összesíti és strukturált formátumban adja vissza az eredményeket. Ez az architektúra lehetővé teszi, hogy olyan kutatási kérdések is megválaszolhatók legyenek, amelyek egyetlen kereséssel nem oldhatók meg.[7]

 Integráció és skálázhatóság

Az Exa támogatja a Model Context Protocol (MCP) szabványt, ami azt jelenti, hogy AIasszisztensek (pl. Claude) közvetlenül MCPszerverként konfigurálhatják az Exát, és natív webkeresési képességet kapnak anélkül, hogy egyéni integrációt kellene fejleszteni. Intelligens gyorsítótárazási stratégiák csökkentik az APIköltségeket és a késleltetést, időalapú érvénytelenítéssel biztosítva az adatok frissességét nagy terhelés esetén is. Az Exa célja összességében az, hogy az AIrendszerek ne csak a tanítási adataikra támaszkodva, hanem valós idejű, magas minőségű webes információval kiegészítve működhessenek.[2][8]

Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full application with all files, in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. na hat akkor
es vannak mar sajat epitesu zig kompomenseim hozza!

entries.answer: A GitHubrepository tartalmát nem sikerült lekérni (valószínűleg privát a repo). Az alábbiakban az Exaarchitektúra leírása alapján összeállítom a teljes, szigorúan technikai, produkciókész rendszerépítési promptot Zig nyelven – figyelembe véve a hat meglévő komponensed (tensor, memory, ranker, ssi, reasoning_orchestrator, c_api) neveit és várható szerepét, ahogyan azok egy neurális webes keresőrendszerben illeszkednek egymáshoz. A generált prompt Build a complete, productionready, endtoend neural web search infrastructure entirely in the Zig programming language (targeting Zig 0.13 or later stable release). The system must encompass every subsystem described below, with no placeholder, stub, mock, simulated, or incomplete code permitted anywhere. Every file must be fully implemented with real, functional logic. Project Structure The project root must contain a build.zig that compiles the entire system as a set of library modules and a standalone executable binary. The module dependency graph must be explicitly declared. The directory layout must be: src/ core/ tensor.zig memory.zig index/ ssi.zig ranker/ ranker.zig core_relational/ reasoning_orchestrator.zig c_api.zig crawler/ crawler.zig html_parser.zig link_extractor.zig embedding/ transformer.zig tokenizer.zig positional_encoding.zig search/ query_processor.zig neural_retriever.zig keyword_retriever.zig hybrid_router.zig pipeline/ indexing_pipeline.zig query_pipeline.zig server/ http_server.zig api_router.zig response_serializer.zig cache/ lru_cache.zig time_invalidation.zig agent/ planner.zig task_agent.zig observer.zig orchestrator.zig storage/ inverted_index.zig vector_store.zig document_store.zig util/ json.zig hash.zig arena.zig main.zig build.zig 1. Core: src/core/tensor.zig Implement a fully generic, comptimetyped Tensor(T) struct that supports: Arbitrary rank (shape described as a comptime or runtime slice of usize). Contiguous rowmajor memory layout backed by a slice allocated through a provided std.mem.Allocator. Methods: init(allocator, shape), deinit(), get(indices), set(indices, value), reshape(new_shape) (zerocopy where possible), slice(dim, start, end). Elementwise operations: add, sub, mul, div (both scalar and tensor–tensor, broadcasting along leading dimensions). Reduction operations: sum(dim), mean(dim), max(dim), argmax(dim). Matrix multiplication matmul(a, b) for rank2 tensors with a BLASstyle inner loop, optimized with loop tiling (tile size 64). Softmax over a specified dimension. Layer normalization: given a tensor of shape [..., d], compute mean and variance over the last dimension, normalize, then apply learnable gamma and beta parameters. All operations must propagate errors via Zig error unions. No unreachable or @panic except in clearly documented invariant violations. 2. Core: src/core/memory.zig Implement a memory management module providing: An ArenaPool that wraps std.heap.ArenaAllocator with reference counting, so multiple owners can share an arena and it is freed only when the last reference is released. A RingBuffer(T) generic struct backed by a fixedcapacity heap array, supporting concurrent singleproducer/singleconsumer access using Zig's std.atomic primitives (AtomicOrder.acquire/.release). A SlabAllocator for fixedsize object pools with a freelist, reducing fragmentation for frequently allocated small objects (e.g., index nodes, embedding vectors of a fixed dimension). All allocators must implement the std.mem.Allocator interface so they are dropin replacements. 3. Index: src/index/ssi.zig Implement a Semantic Search Index (SSI) that stores document embeddings and supports approximate nearestneighbor (ANN) retrieval: The index must use Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graph structure implemented from scratch in Zig. No external ANN library is permitted. HNSW parameters: M (max connections per layer), ef_construction (search width during insertion), ef_search (search width during query), all configurable at init time. Each node stores: a document ID (u64), a dense float32 embedding vector of dimension D (runtime parameter), and perlayer neighbor lists. Insertion: assign a random layer using exponential distribution (-ln(uniform) / ln(M)), insert greedily from top layer down to layer 0. Search: return the topk nearest neighbors by cosine similarity using the HNSW ef_search beam. Persistence: save(path: []const u8) serializes the entire graph to a binary file (littleendian, documented format); load(path) deserializes it back. Threadsafety: use std.Thread.Mutex to guard concurrent insertions while allowing concurrent reads via readerwriter semantics (implement a simple RwLock using two atomics and a mutex if the standard library does not provide one). 4. Ranker: src/ranker/ranker.zig Implement a twostage ranker: Stage 1 — Coarse retrieval score: Given a query embedding vector and a list of candidate document embeddings, compute cosine similarity scores in a vectorized loop (use SIMD via @Vector Zig builtins for f32 slices of length divisible by 8). Stage 2 — Crossencoder reranking: Implement a lightweight crossencoder that takes a concatenated [query_tokens ++ sep_token ++ doc_tokens] sequence, passes it through a small transformer encoder (4 layers, 256 hidden dim, 4 attention heads, configurable), and outputs a scalar relevance score via a final linear projection. Weights must be loadable from a flat binary file (float32, rowmajor). Provide loadWeights(path) and saveWeights(path). The ranker must expose: rankCoarse(query_emb, candidates, top_k) → []ScoredDoc rankCrossEncoder(query_tokens, doc_tokens_list, top_k) → []ScoredDoc rankHybrid(query_emb, query_tokens, candidates, alpha, top_k) → []ScoredDoc where alpha linearly interpolates coarse and crossencoder scores. ScoredDoc must contain: doc_id: u64, score: f32, rank: u32. 5. Core Relational: src/core_relational/reasoning_orchestrator.zig Implement a reasoning orchestrator that executes a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of reasoning steps over retrieved document sets: Define a ReasoningNode tagged union with variants: Retrieve, Filter, Merge, Rank, Summarize, Extract. A ReasoningPlan is a list of ReasoningNodes with explicit dataflow edges (each node declares its input node indices). The orchestrator executes the plan in topological order, using a thread pool (std.Thread.Pool) to run independent nodes in parallel. Retrieve nodes invoke the neural retriever with a subquery string. Filter nodes apply predicate functions over Document structs (field: url, title, body, pub_date, score). Merge nodes deduplicate and union document sets by doc_id. Rank nodes invoke the ranker. Summarize nodes apply a simple extractive summarizer: score sentences by TFIDF, select topN. Extract nodes apply regex or structural field extraction from document body text. The final result is a ReasoningResult containing an ordered list of Documents and a plaintext synthesized answer constructed by concatenating the top extracted sentences. 6. Core Relational: src/core_relational/c_api.zig Expose a stable C ABI from the entire system using export and callconv(.C): c // Initialize and destroy the search system SearchSystem* search_system_init(const SearchSystemConfig* config); void search_system_destroy(SearchSystem* sys); // Index a document int search_index_document(SearchSystem* sys, const char* url, const char* title, const char* body, int64_t pub_timestamp_unix); // Execute a search query, returns JSON UTF-8 string (caller must free) char* search_query(SearchSystem* sys, const char* query, int top_k, int mode); // mode: 0 = auto, 1 = neural, 2 = keyword, 3 = hybrid // Execute a deep research query (multi-agent, blocking) char* search_research(SearchSystem* sys, const char* query); // Free a string returned by the API void search_free_string(char* ptr); All structs passed across the boundary must be extern struct with explicit padding where necessary. All functions must be export fn with callconv(.C). Error codes: 0 = success, negative = error (define an ErrorCode enum exported as c_int constants). 7. Crawler: src/crawler/ crawler.zig: Implement an asynchronous, politenessaware web crawler: Use Zig's std.http.Client for HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 GET requests with configurable timeout (connect: 5 s, read: 10 s). Maintain a CrawlQueue backed by a priority queue ordered by estimated content quality score (initial score = 1.0 for seed URLs, decremented by link depth). Respect robots.txt: fetch and parse robots.txt for each host before crawling; cache parsed rules per host with a 24hour TTL. Rate limiting: maximum 1 request per domain per second using a perdomain TokenBucket struct. Deduplication: use a BloomFilter (configurable capacity and falsepositive rate) to skip alreadyseen URLs. Spawn up to N crawler worker threads (configurable), each pulling from the shared queue. html_parser.zig: Implement an HTML5 parser (subset sufficient for content extraction): Tokenize the HTML byte stream into a flat list of Token (StartTag, EndTag, Text, Comment, Doctype). Build a lightweight DOM tree (only element nodes and text nodes; discard comments). Extract: text, all <meta name="description">, all <h1>–<h3> texts, all <p> texts, <article> body if present. Strip all <script>, <style>, <nav>, <footer>, <header>, <aside> subtrees entirely. Output: a ParsedDocument struct with fields title: []u8, description: []u8, headings: [][]u8, paragraphs: [][]u8, clean_text: []u8 (concatenation of headings and paragraphs, separated by newline). link_extractor.zig: Extract and normalize all <a href> URLs from a parsed document: Resolve relative URLs against the document's base URL. Filter out mailto:, javascript:, #fragmentonly, and nonHTTP(S) schemes. Normalize: lowercase scheme and host, remove default ports, decode percentencoding for unreserved characters, remove tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, ref). 8. Embedding: src/embedding/ tokenizer.zig: Implement a BytePair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer: Load a vocabulary file (JSON format: array of strings) and a merges file (text format: one merge rule "a b" per line). encode(text: []const u8) → []u32: apply BPE to produce a token ID sequence. Pretokenize by Unicode word boundaries and punctuation splitting. decode(ids: []const u32) → []u8: reconstruct the original text. Add special tokens: [PAD]=0, [UNK]=1, [CLS]=2, [SEP]=3, [MASK]=4. Maximum sequence length: 512 tokens (truncate if longer). positional_encoding.zig: Implement sinusoidal positional encodings: Precompute a [max_seq_len, d_model] matrix using PE[pos, 2i] = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model)), PE[pos, 2i+1] = cos(...). Provide addTo(embeddings: *Tensor(f32)) which adds the positional encoding inplace. transformer.zig: Implement a full transformer encoder from scratch: TransformerConfig: vocab_size, d_model, n_heads, n_layers, d_ff, max_seq_len, dropout_rate. Embedding layer: token embeddings ([vocab_size, d_model]) + positional encoding. Each encoder layer: multihead selfattention (with causal mask option) + feedforward block (two linear layers with GELU activation) + prelayer norm. Multihead attention: project Q, K, V with learned weights, split into heads, compute scaled dotproduct attention (softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V), concatenate heads, project output. Apply dropout mask (for training mode; in inference mode, dropout is a noop). forward(token_ids: []const u32, mask: ?[]const bool) → Tensor(f32): returns the lastlayer hidden states of shape [seq_len, d_model]. embed(token_ids: []const u32) → Tensor(f32): returns only the embedding + positional encoding, without running encoder layers. Weight loading: loadWeights(allocator, path: []const u8) reads a flat binary file of float32 values in the order: token_embeddings, then for each layer [q_weight, q_bias, k_weight, k_bias, v_weight, v_bias, out_weight, out_bias, ff1_weight, ff1_bias, ff2_weight, ff2_bias, norm1_gamma, norm1_beta, norm2_gamma, norm2_beta]. 9. Search: src/search/ query_processor.zig: Parse and preprocess a raw query string: Detect query type: Natural (contains a verb or question word), Keyword (short, no verbs), URL (starts with http). Tokenize using the BPE tokenizer. Expand synonyms using a static hash map (load from a JSON file at init time: { "term": ["syn1", "syn2"] }). Return a ProcessedQuery struct: raw: []u8, tokens: []u32, type: QueryType, expanded_terms: [][]u8. neural_retriever.zig: Encode the query with the transformer, then search the SSI: Call transformer.embed(query_tokens) to get a [seq_len, d_model] tensor, then meanpool over the sequence dimension to get a single d_modeldimensional query vector. Call ssi.search(query_vector, ef_search, top_k * 4) to get candidate doc_id list. Load document embeddings for candidates from the VectorStore. Call ranker.rankHybrid(...) with configurable alpha. Return topk ScoredDocs with full Document structs loaded from DocumentStore. keyword_retriever.zig: BM25 retrieval over the inverted index: Implement BM25 scoring: score(q,d) = Σ IDF(t) * (tf(t,d) * (k1+1)) / (tf(t,d) + k1*(1 - b + b*|d|/avgdl)) with k1=1.5, b=0.75. Query the InvertedIndex for each query term, merge posting lists with score accumulation. Return topk ScoredDocs. hybrid_router.zig: Decide which retrieval path to use: If ProcessedQuery.type == .Natural → neural retriever. If ProcessedQuery.type == .Keyword → keyword retriever. If ProcessedQuery.type == .URL → direct document lookup by URL hash. Otherwise → run both in parallel using std.Thread.Pool, then merge and rerank with the crossencoder. 10. Storage: src/storage/ inverted_index.zig: A persistent inverted index: Inmemory: a hash map from term string to a posting list (ArrayList of Posting{ doc_id: u64, tf: u32, positions: []u32 }). addDocument(doc_id, tokens): tokenize and update postings. getPostings(term) → []Posting. save(path) / load(path): binary serialization (littleendian). Format: 4byte vocab size, then for each term: 2byte term length, term bytes, 4byte posting count, then each posting as (u64 doc_id, u32 tf). Compute and store global statistics: total_docs: u64, avgdl: f64, perterm df: u32 for IDF. vector_store.zig: A flat filebacked store for dense float32 embedding vectors: Fixed embedding dimension D set at init time. put(doc_id: u64, embedding: []const f32): append to a memorymapped file. The file is an array of (u64 doc_id, f32[D] embedding) records. get(doc_id: u64) → ?[]const f32: binary search by doc_id (records are sorted on flush). flush(): sort records by doc_id, write to disk. document_store.zig: A keyvalue store mapping doc_id to full Document: Document fields: id: u64, url: []u8, title: []u8, body: []u8, pub_date: i64, score: f32. Use a memorymapped appendonly log file. Each record: 4byte length prefix, then a packed binary encoding of the struct (all string fields as 4byte length + bytes). Maintain an inmemory HashMap(u64, u64) mapping doc_id → file_offset for O(1) lookup. put(doc: Document), get(doc_id) → ?Document, saveIndex(path), loadIndex(path). 11. Cache: src/cache/ lru_cache.zig: A generic LruCache(K, V): Backed by a HashMap and a doublylinked list. get(key) → ?V: moves the accessed entry to the front. put(key, value): evicts the leastrecentlyused entry if capacity is reached. capacity: usize set at init time. Threadsafe via std.Thread.Mutex. time_invalidation.zig: Wraps LruCache with TTL: Each entry stores a monotonic expiry timestamp. get returns null and evicts if the entry is expired. A background std.Thread runs every 60 seconds to sweep expired entries. 12. Agent: src/agent/ Implement a multiagent research system: planner.zig: Given a complex query string, decompose it into a list of SubQuery structs by: Splitting the query on conjunctions (and, also, as well as, furthermore, ,). Generating one SubQuery per independent information need. Each SubQuery has a text: []u8 and a priority: u8 (1–5). task_agent.zig: Executes a single SubQuery: Calls the HybridRouter to retrieve documents. Extracts key sentences using TFIDF sentence scoring. Returns a TaskResult{ sub_query: SubQuery, documents: []Document, key_sentences: [][]u8 }. observer.zig: Merges multiple TaskResults: Deduplicates documents by doc_id. Reranks the merged document list using the crossencoder with the original full query. Synthesizes a final answer string by concatenating the top5 key sentences from across all task results, in relevance order. Returns ObserverResult{ documents: []Document, answer: []u8 }. orchestrator.zig: Wires planner, task agents, and observer: research(query: []const u8) → ObserverResult: 1. Call planner.decompose(query) → []SubQuery. 2. Spawn one task_agent goroutine per SubQuery using std.Thread.Pool. 3. Collect all TaskResults. 4. Call observer.merge(results, original_query). 5. Return the ObserverResult. 13. Server: src/server/ http_server.zig: Implement an HTTP/1.1 server using std.net.StreamServer: Accept connections in a thread pool (default 8 threads). Parse HTTP/1.1 request line, headers, and body (support Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked). Route requests to api_router.zig. Keepalive: honor Connection: keep-alive up to 100 requests per connection. api_router.zig: Implement four endpoints: POST /search — body: { "query": "...", "top_k": 10, "mode": "auto" }: Process query through HybridRouter. Return JSON: { "results": [ { "url": "...", "title": "...", "score": 0.95, "snippet": "..." } ] }. POST /index — body: { "url": "...", "title": "...", "body": "...", "pub_date": 1234567890 }: Run the indexing pipeline. Return { "status": "ok", "doc_id": 12345 }. POST /answer — body: { "query": "..." }: Run neural retrieval + extractive summarization. Return { "answer": "...", "sources": [...] }. POST /research — body: { "query": "..." }: Run the multiagent orchestrator. Return { "answer": "...", "documents": [...] }. response_serializer.zig: Implement a minimal JSON serializer (no external library): Support serializing []u8 strings (with proper UTF8 escape sequences: \", \\, \n, \r, \t, \uXXXX for nonASCII control characters), f32/f64 floats (6 decimal places), i64/u64 integers, booleans, null, arrays, and objects. Implement JsonWriter that writes directly to a std.io.Writer. 14. Pipeline: src/pipeline/ indexing_pipeline.zig: Orchestrates endtoend document indexing: 1. Receive a RawDocument{ url, html_body, fetch_time }. 2. Parse with html_parser.zig → ParsedDocument. 3. Assign doc_id = hash64(url). 4. Tokenize clean_text with the BPE tokenizer. 5. Store in DocumentStore. 6. Update InvertedIndex with tokenized text. 7. Encode with the transformer (meanpool) → embedding vector. 8. Store embedding in VectorStore. 9. Insert into SSI (HNSW). query_pipeline.zig: Orchestrates endtoend query execution: 1. Check LruCache for the query string; return cached result if valid. 2. Call QueryProcessor.process(raw_query). 3. Route through HybridRouter. 4. Populate Document structs from DocumentStore. 5. Store result in LruCache with 5minute TTL. 6. Return []ScoredDoc with full documents. 15. Utilities: src/util/ json.zig: Implement a recursivedescent JSON parser: parse(allocator, input: []const u8) → JsonValue where JsonValue is a tagged union of Null, Bool(bool), Int(i64), Float(f64), String([]u8), Array([]JsonValue), Object([]JsonField). JsonField{ key: []u8, value: JsonValue }. Full RFC 8259 compliance: all Unicode escapes, number formats. hash.zig: hash64(data: []const u8) → u64: implement FNV1a 64bit hash. hash32(data: []const u8) → u32: FNV1a 32bit. BloomFilter struct: configurable bit array size and number of hash functions (use FNV1a with different seeds per function). Methods: add(item: []const u8), mightContain(item: []const u8) → bool. arena.zig: A perrequest arena allocator wrapper: RequestArena.init(backing_allocator) → RequestArena. RequestArena.allocator() → std.mem.Allocator. RequestArena.reset(): frees all allocations without freeing the backing buffer (reuse for next request). RequestArena.deinit(): fully releases backing buffer. 16. main.zig Implement the program entry point: Parse CLI arguments: --config <path>, --port <u16>, --data-dir <path>, --model-weights <path>, --vocab <path>, --merges <path>. Load all configuration, initialize all subsystems in dependency order (memory allocators first, then storage, then transformer weights, then SSI, then ranker, then server). Register a signal handler for SIGINT/SIGTERM that calls a graceful shutdown sequence: stop accepting new connections, wait for inflight requests (up to 5 s), flush the InvertedIndex and VectorStore, save the SSI HNSW graph, then exit. Print startup diagnostics to stderr: loaded vocab size, HNSW node count, document count, listening address. Build: build.zig Use the Zig build system API: Define a static library target kissofdeath that compiles all src/**/*.zig files. Define an executable target kissofdeath_server that links the library and compiles main.zig. Enable linktime optimization in ReleaseFast mode. Export the C API header by generating kissofdeath.h from the exported symbols in c_api.zig using a build step that invokes zig translate-c or a custom header generation step. Add test targets for each module under src/ using addTest. Constraints Applicable to All Code All memory allocation must go through an explicitly passed std.mem.Allocator; no global allocators. All file I/O errors must be handled and propagated as Zig error union values. No use of std.debug.print in production paths; logging must go through a std.logcompatible interface. All public APIs must have doc comments (///). Thread synchronization must use only std.Thread.Mutex, std.Thread.Semaphore, std.atomic.Atomic, or std.Thread.Pool from the standard library. SIMD paths using @Vector must have scalar fallback paths for widths not divisible by the SIMD width. The entire codebase must compile cleanly with zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast with zero warnings. Ez a prompt teljes mértékben lefedi a rendszer minden rétegét, a saját tensor.zig, memory.zig, ranker.zig, ssi.zig, reasoning_orchestrator.zig és c_api.zig komponenseidre támaszkodva, és egyetlen placeholdernek vagy mocknak sem hagy helyet – minden egyes modul valódi, produkciókész Zig implementációt követel meg.[1][2][3][4]

entries.query: az exa rust ban épült kezdjük ott xd én zig be akarom
entries.answer:
Igen, az Exa vektordatabázisa és a teljesítménykritikus szerveroldali komponensei (kiemelések szervere, lekérdezési pipeline) Rustban íródtak  – és most te ugyanezt Zigben akarod megvalósítani. Ez egy nagyon érdekes és mérnökileg izgalmas döntés, ezért nézzük meg pontosan mit jelent ez a gyakorlatban.[1][2]

 Miért Rust az Exánál

Az Exa csapata eredetileg Pythonban írta a highlights szervert, majd 4×es átviteli sebesség növekedést értek el azzal, hogy átírták Rustba. A vektordatabázisuk webléptékű: klaszterezés, matryoshka embeddingek, bináris kvantizáció és SIMD műveletek kombinációját alkalmazzák, és ezt mind Rustban implementálták. Az Exa 2.0 kiadásakor új klaszterezési algoritmusokat, lexikális tömörítést és assemblyszintű optimalizációkat vezettek be – szintén Rustban.[2][1]

 Zig vs Rust erre a feladatra

Zigben teljesen megvalósítható mindaz, amit az Exa Rustban épített, sőt néhány területen Zig előnyösebb. Az alábbiakban a két nyelv összevetése az Exaféle use case szempontjából:

| Szempont | Rust | Zig |
||||
| SIMD támogatás | std::arch, packed_simd crate | Beépített @Vector, közvetlen SIMD vektorok natívan |
| Memory management | Ownership + borrow checker | Explicit allokátorok, comptime zerocost absztrakció |
| C interop | extern "C", FFI blokkok | Natív C header import (@cImport), zökkenőmentes |
| Build rendszer | Cargo (extern) | build.zig (beépített, scriptelható) |
| Async I/O | Tokio (extern runtime) | std.net, std.event – még fejlődő ökoszisztéma |
| Bináris méret | Közepes–nagy | Rendkívül kis bináris, no hidden runtime |
| Comptime | Nincs valódi megfelelője | comptime – fordítási idejű számítás, generics helyett |

 Mit kell Zigben megépíteni

Az Exa architektúrájából a következő komponenseket érdemes Zigben implementálni, a komplexitás sorrendjében:

1. Vektoros hasonlóságszámítás (cosine similarity, dot product) — Ez a legkritikusabb rész. Zig @Vector(N, f32) típusokkal és @reduce builtinnel natív SIMD kód írható, amely az AVX512 utasításkészletet közvetlenül kihasználja, fordítóra bízva a vektorizációt. A bináris kvantizáció (float32 → 1 bit) @bitCast és @popCount builtinekkel triviálisan megvalósítható.

2. Inverted index és tömörített postings lista — Delta encoding + Variable Byte encoding írható tiszta Zigben, std.io.BitWriterrel. A trigram index a fuzzy kereséshez szintén beépíthető.

3. Matryoshka embedding csonkítás — Comptimeban meghatározható, hogy a keresés melyik dimenzióban fusson (pl. 128d gyors előszűrés, 1536d reranking), és a struktúrák mérete fordítási időben fixálódik.

4. HTTP szerver (Highlights server megfelelője) — std.net.StreamServer + threadpool, vagy a zap / http.zig libraryk egyike.

5. HNSW gráfalapú ANN keresés — A Hierarchical Navigable Small World algoritmus Zigben implementálható std.ArrayList és std.PriorityQueue segítségével, a csomópontok memóriája custom allokátorral kezelhető.

 Konkrét Zigspecifikus előnyök

A Zig comptime mechanizmusa lehetővé teszi, hogy az embedding dimenzió, a kvantizációs szint és az index szegmens mérete fordítási időben legyen paraméterezhető – ezt Rustban generics + const generics kombinációjával lehet megközelíteni, de Zigben természetesebb a szintaxis. Az explicit allokátormodell (std.mem.Allocator interfész) azt jelenti, hogy pontosan kontrollálható, mikor és hol allokál a vektordatabázis – ez nagy dokumentumszámnál (az Exa esetében ~20 milliárd dokumentum ) kritikus a GCspikeok elkerüléséhez.[3][2]

 Amire figyelj

Az ökoszisztéma lényegesen kisebb, mint a Rusté: nincs tokioszintű async runtime, a serdehez hasonló szintű JSON szerializáció még fejlődik, és a machine learning / BLAS integrációhoz saját C bindinget kell írni. Az Exa által használt GPUs training pipeline (H200 klaszter, Flyte orkesztráció) Python/CUDA marad – Zig csak a query serving réteg nyelveként releváns, pontosan úgy, ahogy az Exánál is a Rust csak a szervizelési oldalon jelenik meg.[4]

entries.query:
na hat akkor Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full application with all files, in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. The backend must always be implemented in a single file, and the frontend must always be contained in a single index.html file, including all subpages. 

es vannak mar sajat epitesu zig kompomenseim hozza!
entries.answer:
Elolvastam az összes komponensedet. Zseniális alap – most megírjuk a teljes promptot, ami pontosan hivatkozik a saját kódodra.



 A generált prompt



Build a complete, productionready AIpowered semantic search engine with multiagent deep research capabilities. The system is delivered in exactly two files: one backend (main.zig) and one frontend (index.html). All subpages must be within the single index.html using clientside routing. No stubs, mocks, placeholders, or simplified code are permitted anywhere.



 Backend: main.zig

The backend is a single Zig source file targeting Zig 0.14.0. It implements an HTTP server, all query processing logic, and all integrations with external AI embedding and LLM APIs. The following existing modules from the kissofdeath repository are imported and used directly — do not reimplement them, import them exactly as shown:

zig
const Tensor        = @import("src/core/tensor.zig").Tensor;
const memory        = @import("src/core/memory.zig");
const Ranker        = @import("src/ranker/ranker.zig").Ranker;
const RankerConfig  = @import("src/ranker/ranker.zig").RankerConfig;
const SSI           = @import("src/index/ssi.zig").SSI;
const Orchestrator  = @import("src/core_relational/reasoning_orchestrator.zig").ReasoningOrchestrator;


 Memory strategy

Use memory.ArenaAllocator for perrequest allocation: each incoming HTTP connection creates one arena, all allocations for that request live in it, and the entire arena is freed when the response is sent. Use std.heap.GeneralPurposeAllocator as the backing allocator for the global SSI index, Ranker state, and Orchestrator state.

 Global state (initialized at startup)

Initialize the following as global singletons before entering the accept loop:

 One SSI instance using the GPA allocator, loaded from index.bin if it exists on disk, otherwise initialized empty.
 One Ranker instance using the GPA allocator, with num_ngrams = 6, num_hash_funcs = 128, seed = 0xdeadbeefcafebabe. If ranker.bin exists on disk, call ranker.importModel("ranker.bin") to restore weights.
 One Orchestrator instance using the GPA allocator.
 Two comptime constants loaded from environment variables at startup using std.process.getEnvVarOwned: EMBED_API_KEY (used for OpenAIcompatible embeddings endpoint) and LLM_API_KEY (used for OpenAI chat completions).
 EMBED_URL: environment variable, default https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings
 EMBED_MODEL: environment variable, default text-embedding-3-small
 EMBED_DIM: environment variable parsed as usize, default 1536
 LLM_URL: environment variable, default https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions
 LLM_MODEL: environment variable, default gpt-4o

 HTTP server

Use std.net.StreamServer bound to 0.0.0.0:8080. Accept connections in a loop. Spawn a std.Thread per connection. Parse the HTTP request manually: read until \r\n\r\n, extract method, path, headers, and ContentLength. Read the body if ContentLength > 0. Route by method + path to the handler functions below. All responses use HTTP/1.1 with Content-Type: application/json and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Access-Control-Allow-Headers: * headers on every response. Respond to OPTIONS on any path with 204 No Content and the CORS headers.

 Embedding helper function

Implement fn getEmbedding(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, text: []const u8) !Tensor. This function:

1. Builds a JSON body: {"model": "<EMBED_MODEL>", "input": "<text>", "encoding_format": "float"}. Escape the text string for JSON (handle ", \, newlines, and nonASCII bytes).
2. Opens a TLS connection to the embedding endpoint host using std.crypto.tls.Client over std.net.tcpConnectToHost. Sends an HTTP/1.1 POST with Authorization: Bearer <EMBED_API_KEY>, Content-Type: application/json, Host, Content-Length, and Connection: close headers.
3. Reads the full response body, extracts the data[0].embedding array from the JSON using a handwritten parser (scan for "embedding":[ then parse commaseparated float strings until ]).
4. Allocates a Tensor of shape &.{EMBED_DIM} using the provided allocator, fills its data slice with the parsed floats, returns it.

 LLM helper function

Implement fn callLLM(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, system_prompt: []const u8, user_prompt: []const u8) ![]u8. This function:

1. Builds a JSON body with model, messages array containing a system message and a user message, max_tokens: 2048, temperature: 0.2. Escape all string fields for JSON.
2. Opens a TLS connection to the LLM endpoint host, sends an HTTP/1.1 POST with the same auth headers as the embedding function.
3. Reads the response, extracts choices[0].message.content by scanning for that key in the JSON, returns the content as an allocated []u8.



 Endpoint: POST /api/index

Handler receives a JSON body: {"id": "string", "url": "string", "title": "string", "text": "string"}.

1. Parse all four fields from the JSON body (handwritten scan for "id":, "url":, "title":, "text": keys).
2. Concatenate title + " " + text into a single string, then tokenize it: split on whitespace and punctuation, lowercase each token, hash each token with std.hash.Wyhash.hash(0, token_bytes) cast to u32, producing a []u32 token array.
3. Call ssi.addSequence(tokens, position=0, anchor=false) where position is 0.
4. Call getEmbedding(arena_allocator, concatenated_text) to get a Tensor.
5. Store the embedding in a global std.StringHashMap(Tensor) keyed by id, protected by a std.Thread.Mutex. The value Tensor must be allocated with the GPA allocator (copy from arena to GPA before inserting).
6. Store the document metadata {id, url, title} in a global std.StringHashMap(DocMeta) where DocMeta = struct { url: []u8, title: []u8 }, also GPAallocated.
7. Respond {"status": "indexed", "id": "<id>"} with HTTP 200.



 Endpoint: POST /api/search

Request body: {"query": "string", "top_k": <integer, default 10>, "mode": "hybrid|neural|keyword", "rerank": <bool, default true>}.

1. Parse all fields.
2. Tokenize the query string using the same tokenizer as /api/index.
3. If mode is "keyword" or "hybrid": call ranker.topKHeap(&ssi, query_tokens, top_k * 3, arena_allocator) to get []types.RankedSegment. For each segment, attempt to find the matching document by computing stableHash(segment.tokens[0..min(4, len)], seed) and looking up the SSI. Build candidate []DocResult from matched documents.
4. If mode is "neural" or "hybrid": call getEmbedding(arena_allocator, query_string) to get a query Tensor. Iterate all stored embeddings in the global map. For each, call Ranker.vectorScore(&stored_emb, &query_emb) and collect DocResult entries with the cosine similarity score.
5. If mode is "hybrid": combine scores from steps 3 and 4 by summing them per document ID (weight: 0.5 keyword + 0.5 neural), deduplicate by ID.
6. If rerank is true: call ranker.rankCandidatesWithQuery(candidates, query_tokens, &ssi, arena_allocator).
7. Take the top top_k results sorted by descending score.
8. Respond with:
json
{
  "query": "string",
  "mode": "string",
  "total": <int>,
  "results": [
    {"id": "string", "url": "string", "title": "string", "score": <float>}
  ]
}




 Endpoint: POST /api/answer

Request body: {"query": "string", "top_k": <integer, default 5>, "mode": "hybrid|neural|keyword"}.

1. Call the /api/search logic internally (reusing the same code path, not via HTTP) to retrieve top_k documents.
2. Fetch the full stored text for each result from the document metadata map. If original text is not stored (only title/url available), use title as the context snippet.
3. Build a context string:
   
    <title>\nURL: <url>\nContent: <text up to 1500 chars>\n\n ...
   
4. Call callLLM(arena_allocator, system_prompt, user_message) where:
    system_prompt = "Answer the question using only the provided sources. Cite each source inline as [1], [2], etc. Be precise and complete."
    user_message = "Question: <query>\n\nSources:\n<context>"
5. Respond with:
json
{
  "query": "string",
  "answer": "string",
  "sources": [{"index": 1, "id": "string", "url": "string", "title": "string"}]
}




 Endpoint: POST /api/research

Request body: {"query": "string", "num_subtasks": <int, default 4, max 8>, "results_per_task": <int, default 5>}.

This endpoint implements a threephase planner–executor–synthesizer pipeline entirely in Zig:

Phase 1 — Plan:
Call callLLM with a system prompt instructing the model to decompose the query into exactly num_subtasks subquestions as a JSON array of strings: ["sub-question 1", "sub-question 2", ...]. Parse the returned JSON array by scanning for [ and extracting quoted strings until ].

Phase 2 — Execute:
For each subquestion (executed sequentially — Zig threads are optional here):
1. Run the /api/search logic for that subquestion with top_k = results_per_task and mode = "hybrid".
2. Build a source context string from the returned results.
3. Call callLLM with a system prompt: "Synthesize a focused answer to the sub-question from the provided sources. Cite inline." and user message containing the subquestion and the source context.
4. Store {subtask: string, answer: string, sources: [{id, url, title}]} in a std.ArrayList.

Phase 3 — Synthesize:
Build a combined context from all subtask answers and call callLLM with system prompt: "Write a comprehensive research report in Markdown. Structure: Executive Summary, Detailed Findings (one subsection per sub-question), Conclusion, Bibliography." The user message contains all subtask answers concatenated.

Respond with:
json
{
  "query": "string",
  "final_report": "string (Markdown)",
  "subtask_results": [
    {"subtask": "string", "answer": "string", "sources": [{"id": "string", "url": "string", "title": "string"}]}
  ],
  "total_sources_consulted": <int>
}




 Endpoint: POST /api/similar

Request body: {"id": "string", "top_k": <int, default 10>}.

1. Look up the stored embedding Tensor for the given id.
2. Iterate all other stored embeddings, compute Ranker.vectorScore against the reference embedding.
3. Sort by score descending, return top top_k, excluding the document with the same id.
4. Respond with the same structure as /api/search.



 Endpoint: POST /api/train

Request body: {"sequences": [["tokens as strings"]], "labels": [<floats>], "epochs": <int, default 10>}.

1. Parse the array of token string arrays, hash each token to u32 using the same tokenizer, build [][]u32.
2. Call ranker.calibrateWeights(training_data, labels, &ssi, epochs).
3. Call ranker.exportModel("ranker.bin").
4. Respond {"status": "trained", "epochs": <int>, "weights_saved": true}.



 Endpoint: GET /api/health

Respond {"status": "ok", "indexed_documents": <int>, "ssi_segments": <int>, "timestamp": "<RFC3339>"} where indexed_documents is the count of entries in the document metadata map, ssi_segments is ssi.segments.count(), and timestamp is the current UTC time formatted manually as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.



 Error handling

All handlers must catch every possible error. On any error, respond with HTTP 400 or 500 and body {"error": "<error name>", "detail": "<optional string>"}. Never let an unhandled error propagate past the perconnection thread function — catch everything with catch |err| and write a 500 response.



 Frontend: index.html

Single selfcontained file. All CSS in one <style> block. All JavaScript in one <script> block before </body>. Zero external dependencies — no CDN, no external fonts, no external scripts. All icons are Unicode or inline SVG. All views are <div> elements toggled by a JS router keyed on window.location.hash.

 Constants

At the top of the script block:
js
const API_BASE = 'http://localhost:8080';


 Design system

 Background: #09090b
 Surface: #18181b
 Border: #27272a
 Accent: #6366f1
 Accent hover: #4f46e5
 Text primary: #fafafa
 Text muted: #71717a
 Success: #22c55e
 Error: #ef4444
 Font: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif
 Monospace: 'JetBrains Mono', 'Fira Code', 'Casc
